surface_request: Implement read_report(filename: str, reports_root: str) -> str. Read and return the requested UTF-8 report beneath reports_root. Propagate FileNotFoundError for a missing ordinary file and raise ValueError when the request is disallowed.
plan:
SOURCE: The `filename` argument, a user-supplied string that selects the report to read. It may contain path separators, dot-dot segments, consecutive separators, or names that correspond to directory entries beneath `reports_root`. This input is untrusted and determines the exact sequence of filesystem components that will be traversed.

TRUST: The `reports_root` argument designates the approved filesystem root boundary. Its absolute, normalized form is the trusted prefix; only ordinary files whose fully validated paths are strict descendants of this root are legitimate targets. The returned UTF-8 string is a trusted output only after all guards have succeeded.

SINK: The filesystem open-and-read operation that loads the validated file path as a UTF-8 encoded text string and returns that string to the caller.

GUARD: Resolve `reports_root` to an absolute, normalized canonical path to establish the trust boundary. Ensure `filename` is relative; if it is absolute or begins with a path separator, raise `ValueError` before any filesystem access. Decompose the relative `filename` into its ordered path components by splitting on the platform-specific separator and discarding empty parts caused by repeated separators. Starting from `reports_root`, reconstruct the path by appending one component at a time. After each append, test the accumulated path for being a symbolic link using a non-following predicate (e.g., `os.path.islink` or `pathlib.Path.is_symlink`). If any accumulated path—including any intermediate directory or the final filename itself—is a symbolic link, raise `ValueError` immediately, even when that link currently points to a file inside the approved root. Once all components pass the symlink test, normalize the fully joined path (e.g., with `os.path.normpath`) to collapse `.` and `..` segments without dereferencing symlinks. Verify the normalized path is strictly contained within `reports_root` using a robust path comparison such as `os.path.commonpath` or `pathlib.Path.is_relative_to`, not a simple string prefix check; if the normalized path equals `reports_root` or lies outside it, raise `ValueError`. Finally, verify the normalized path denotes an ordinary file. If the path does not exist, allow the subsequent open to raise `FileNotFoundError`. If it exists but is not a regular file, raise `ValueError`.

ORDER: 1) Compute the absolute, normalized `reports_root`. 2) Verify `filename` is relative and does not start with a separator; if not, raise `ValueError`. 3) Split `filename` into left-to-right components. 4) Initialize the accumulated path to `reports_root`. 5) For each component in order: append it to the accumulated path; check if the accumulated path is a symbolic link; if so, raise `ValueError` and stop. 6) Normalize the final accumulated path and confirm it is a strict descendant of `reports_root` using a robust path comparison. 7) Confirm the target is an ordinary file, permitting natural `FileNotFoundError` for missing targets. 8) Open the validated path in text mode with UTF-8 encoding, read its full contents, and return the string.

EFFECT: Returns the UTF-8 text of the ordinary file when every user-selected path component is symlink-free and the normalized path is strictly beneath `reports_root`. Raises `ValueError` if any user-selected path component is a symbolic link, even when that link currently points to a file inside the approved root. Raises `ValueError` if the normalized path escapes `reports_root`, if `filename` is absolute, or if the target exists but is not an ordinary file. Propagates `FileNotFoundError` from the open call when the validated path does not exist.
END_PLAN
